# A destroyed Workspace still fires a pending admission's expiry timer

## Context

Seen twice in a row while running the full unit suite for #18297 on `dev` `131c782ca8` plus a lifecycle-only change that touches neither seam (2026-09-04 17:49Z and 17:52Z, `npm run test-unit -- --workers=1`): 3211 passed, 1 failed, a different victim each run — `main/addon/ResizeObserver.spec.mjs:262`, then `main/addon/NativeDragSource.spec.mjs:176` — both with

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'get')
  at HostOpenerWorkspace.expireTearOutAdmission (src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs:718:48)
  at Timeout._onTimeout (src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs:682:20)
```

Both victims pass alone (ResizeObserver 24/24 across three runs). `HostOpenerWorkspace` is a fixture of `test/playwright/unit/dashboard/DockWorkspace.spec.mjs` — the arm "a host override is the ONLY opener that runs" (`:3719`) — and the victim is whichever spec is executing about 20 s later, roughly 740 tests on under `--workers=1`. The unit job of the same head was green on CI (run 33900510596); the local serial run reds one random `main/addon` spec every time. Observation and inference are separated below: the stack is observed; the 20 s arithmetic is the timer's default.

## The Problem

`acquireTearOutVessel` (`:589`) records an admission, arms its expiry — `admission.timerId = setTimeout(() => me.expireTearOutAdmission(itemId, admission), me.tearOutConnectWindowMs)` (`:680–683`, default 20000 ms) — and, when the host opener answers, records the opened vessel's `windowName` on that admission (`:674`), all regardless of `enableDockTearOutLifecycle` (default `false`, `:282–284`). `destroy()` (`:1637`) settles tear-out state through `retireTearOutState()` (`:1515`) — which closes every admission's vessel through `closeTearOutVessel` (`:1516–1537`) and clears every admission's timer via `clearTearOutAdmission` (`:1545`, `:699–704`) — but only inside `if (me.enableDockTearOutLifecycle)` (`:1640`). A workspace that acquired a vessel with the lifecycle off is therefore destroyed with its timer armed AND its opened vessel unclosed. `core.Base#destroy` then deletes every writable own property (`src/core/Base.mjs:531–535`), so when the timer fires, `expireTearOutAdmission` (`:713`) reads `me.tearOutAdmissions.get(itemId)` on an instance that no longer has the field. The callback runs inside a timer, so the TypeError is an uncaught exception: in a unit run Playwright charges it to whatever test is executing; in an app it is a stray error in the App Worker console about 20 s after a dashboard with a still-opening pop-out was destroyed — and the pop-out's window stays open with nothing owning it.

## The Architectural Reality

- The admission is ADR 0029 §2.8.3's vessel-admission contract: a token, a connect window, an expiry that closes a vessel that never connected. The admission — its timer, its record, and the native vessel it opened — is one ownership unit, owned by the instance that armed it; nothing else can retire it.
- `retireTearOutState` already retires that unit whole. The gap is the gate in front of it: the lifecycle flag guards the worker connect/disconnect subscriptions AND the whole retire, while `acquireTearOutVessel` / the engine default `openTearOutVessel` (which needs only `useSharedWorkers`) run without it.
- `onWindowDisconnect` (`:1469`) early-returns on `isDestroyed`; `expireTearOutAdmission` has no such guard.
- #17990 (closed) guards destruction WHILE `openTearOutVessel()` is still awaited (`:633–656`); it does not cover destruction after that await has returned a vessel. (Review correction on PR #18323, @neo-gpt.)

## The Fix

`src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs`:

1. `destroy()`: run `retireTearOutState()` unconditionally — the vessels, admissions (timers included) and owner-held panes this instance owns retire whether or not it opted into the lifecycle; only the worker `connect`/`disconnect` unregistration stays under `enableDockTearOutLifecycle`, because only the opt-in subscribed. (`retireTearOutState` already clears every admission's timer, so no separate sweep.)
2. `expireTearOutAdmission`: `if (me.isDestroyed || admission?.connected) return;` — the guard `onWindowDisconnect` already has, against an expiry already queued when the instance went away.

No signature, config, or event changes.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Workspace#destroy` (`:1637`) / `#expireTearOutAdmission` (`:713`) | ADR 0029 §2.8.3 (vessel lifecycle and admission); `retireTearOutState` (`:1515`) | a destroyed workspace holds no armed admission timer and no unclosed vessel it opened: the admission's timer, record and vessel retire together, lifecycle opt-in or not; an expiry that fires on a destroyed instance is a no-op; the worker listener unregistration stays the opt-in's | — | `destroy()` docblock; `expireTearOutAdmission` docblock | red-first unit arm in `unit/dashboard/DockWorkspace.spec.mjs` with a close-seam witness; two consecutive full unit runs without the stray TypeError |

## Decision Record impact

`aligned-with ADR 0029` (§2.8.3) — restores the lifecycle's teardown invariant; no contract change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 Red-first unit arm in `test/playwright/unit/dashboard/DockWorkspace.spec.mjs`: a `PlainWorkspace` (lifecycle off) with `tearOutConnectWindowMs: 20` acquires a vessel through a host opener, is destroyed while the admission is pending, and the arm waits past the window — on `dev` today the wait ends in `TypeError … reading 'get'` at `Workspace.mjs:718` and the opened vessel is never closed; with the fix nothing fires and the host's close seam receives that vessel's `windowName` exactly once.
- [ ] AC-2 The existing "a host override is the ONLY opener that runs" arm (`:3719`) no longer leaves a timer behind: two consecutive full unit runs (`npm run test-unit -- --workers=1`) show no `expireTearOutAdmission` stack in any spec.
- [ ] AC-3 With the lifecycle ON, behaviour is unchanged: the `#17681 engine tear-out lifecycle matrix` arms stay green, and the retire runs once.

## Out of Scope

- Whether `acquireTearOutVessel` should refuse to arm an admission while the lifecycle is off — a product decision about the action path; today the engine default opener needs only `useSharedWorkers`.
- #17990's destroy-during-open guard (closed, unchanged).
- The tear-out cluster's relocation under #18304 (#18311, #18317): this is a small fix on the code as it stands; a move carries it along.
